entities.name: Carbonyl-to-alcohol reduction
observations: The product retains the reactant skeleton but changes a terminal carbonyl C=O into C–O, consistent with reduction of an aldehyde or ketone to an alcohol.
Likely reagent classes include sodium borohydride, lithium aluminum hydride, borane, or catalytic hydrogenation depending on chemoselectivity and substrate sensitivity.

entities.name: NaBH4 reduction
observations: Sodium borohydride in an alcohol solvent such as methanol or ethanol is a common mild reagent set for aldehyde/ketone-to-alcohol reduction.

entities.name: LiAlH4 reduction
observations: Lithium aluminum hydride in an ether solvent followed by aqueous workup is a stronger reagent set for carbonyl-to-alcohol reduction.

entities.name: Borane reduction
observations: Borane complexes such as BH3·THF can reduce carbonyl compounds to alcohols and may be considered when other reducible groups are present.
